response.explanation: The operator designates sources/decision.md as the governing current agreement. That decision requires the restore slug to collapse every non-alphanumeric character (ASCII a-z, A-Z, 0-9 preserved; every other UTF-16 code unit becomes one dash, so an astral character becomes two dashes) and states that NFC normalization does not apply to the session path. The public entry point code/restore.py delegates encoding to code/slug.py via `from .slug import encode_project`; the encoder only does `project.replace("/", "-").replace(".", "-")`. It leaves spaces, underscores, other punctuation and all non-ASCII characters untouched and does not perform per-UTF-16-code-unit replacement, so restore_path does not satisfy the governing rule for any project path containing such characters. No caller or guard in restore.py compensates. knowledge/module.md is also stale: it cites sources/proposal.md as its source and states 'replace slashes and dots only. Normalize Unicode to NFC', which matches the unapproved proposal rather than the decision (the proposal itself says it 'has not been adopted'). Because the operator has already selected the governing source, this is not a sources_conflict; the knowledge contradiction is secondary to the code defect.
